DISABLED PEOPLE DENIED VOTING RIGHTS, GROUP SAYS

I work with people who are developmentally disabled. I do not think the majority need to vote simply because the vast majority of the people I work with would vote based on what their caregivers, parents, or other authority figure in their life prompted them to. Unless the person is capable of tending to their own day to day affairs such as money management and scheduling, not physical activities but skills that attest to their cognitive abilities allowing these people to vote would simply be giving the people who manage their lives the ability to vote more than once. For example: in my agency the majority of the employees and family are church of God supporters, therefore the clients are church of God supporters. If they could vote the county the agency is located would have over 100 more voters that would vote for the preposterous regulations and laws the church of God supports. Also, the clients would be shuttled to and from voting on the taxpayers dime while able bodied citizens do not even get election day off work. It would be unfair to people who are cognitive and functioning members of society to allow special needs people to vote.
